description: Task queue pop_next ignores cancellation flags set during queue residency, causing cancelled jobs to execute.
spec_notes: SafeTaskQueue.pop_next must ensure cancelled jobs return with CANCELLED status.

"""Job task definition and status."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable, Optional


@dataclass
class TaskJob:
    job_id: str
    fn: Callable[[], Any]
    status: str = "QUEUED"
    result: Optional[Any] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None

tests.test_task_executor.py:
from models import TaskJob
from task_queue import SafeTaskQueue
from executor import TaskExecutor


def test_fifo_execution():
    q = SafeTaskQueue()
    ex = TaskExecutor(q)
    q.push(TaskJob("j1", lambda: 10))
    q.push(TaskJob("j2", lambda: 20))
    count = ex.drain_and_run()
    assert count == 2
    assert ex.completed["j1"].result == 10
    assert ex.completed["j2"].result == 20


def test_cancelled_job_is_skipped_without_running_fn():
    q = SafeTaskQueue()
    ex = TaskExecutor(q)
    ran_flag = False
    def side_effect():
        nonlocal ran_flag
        ran_flag = True
        return "BAD"

    q.push(TaskJob("j_cancel", side_effect))
    res = q.cancel("j_cancel")
    assert res is True
    count = ex.drain_and_run()
    assert count == 0
    assert ran_flag is False
    assert ex.completed["j_cancel"].status == "CANCELLED"
    assert ex.completed["j_cancel"].result is None


def test_cancel_nonexistent_job():
    q = SafeTaskQueue()
    assert q.cancel("missing") is False


def test_failed_job_records_error():
    q = SafeTaskQueue()
    ex = TaskExecutor(q)
    def will_crash():
        raise ValueError("corrupt payload")

    q.push(TaskJob("j_err", will_crash))
    count = ex.drain_and_run()
    assert count == 0
    assert ex.completed["j_err"].status == "FAILED"
    assert "corrupt payload" in ex.completed["j_err"].error


def test_multiple_jobs_with_interleaved_cancellation():
    q = SafeTaskQueue()
    ex = TaskExecutor(q)
    q.push(TaskJob("a", lambda: "A"))
    q.push(TaskJob("b", lambda: "B"))
    q.push(TaskJob("c", lambda: "C"))
    q.cancel("b")
    count = ex.drain_and_run()
    assert count == 2
    assert ex.completed["a"].status == "COMPLETED"
    assert ex.completed["b"].status == "CANCELLED"
    assert ex.completed["c"].status == "COMPLETED"


def test_empty_queue_drain():
    q = SafeTaskQueue()
    ex = TaskExecutor(q)
    assert ex.drain_and_run() == 0
